name: jnethack
why: A Japanese localization of NetHack, a legendary roguelike; the localization angle is a modest curiosity.

brief.what_it_is: JNetHack is a Japanese localization of NetHack, the classic terminal roguelike. Per its README, it is NetHack translated into Japanese, and it is distributed as source that you build into a playable binary named jnethack. Player input for wishes and genocide prompts accepts only Japanese text. Runtime input and output use Shift_JIS, or UTF-8 by default on Mac/UNIX builds since version 3.4 changes. The README is written entirely in Japanese.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation beyond stating what it is (NetHack made Japanese, JNETHACKはNetHackを日本語化したものです。). It is a localization for Japanese-speaking players.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain game mechanics; it is NetHack with translated text. Development uses two repositories: jnethack-release holds source that has been checked, and is rarely rebased; jnethack-alpha holds work in progress, is rebased often, and is built in CI on Travis CI, AppVeyor and GitHub Actions.
brief.install_notes: The README points to japanese/build.md for build instructions, but that path returned HTTP 404 on the release repo, so build steps are unverified. Per the README, the 3.4 source distribution is Shift_JIS and UNIX builds need conversion to EUC-JP first; the 3.6 source is UTF-8 and needs no pre-conversion. On Windows, the config file is .jnethackrc. On Mac/UNIX the default I/O encoding is UTF-8, and the kcode option changes it. Homebrew's description and executable name (jnethack) were the only install details I had.
brief.standout: The localization carries Japanese-specific choices: wish and genocide prompts accept only Japanese input, and the encoding story has changed across versions (Shift_JIS source, then UTF-8 source with Shift_JIS runtime). It is a modest curiosity rather than a technical marvel, per the scout notes.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows a release note for a crash-bug fix, and CI badges, but no version number, release date, or last-commit date was visible in what I could read. The alpha repo page returned the same README text.
brief.caveats: Per the README, the current release only supports windows/tty, so there is no Mac or Linux graphical target. Some parts are still untranslated, and compile warnings remain. The build guide link returned 404. Documentation is in Japanese only; I found no English README. The license was not visible in what I read.
